title: Ind-smoothness lifts along nilpotent thickenings of the base
statement: Let $R\to\Lambda$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Assume (1) $I$ is nilpotent ($I^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$), (2) $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/I$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras], and (3) $R\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Proposition Tag 07CM (proposition-lift, line 1374) and its proof (induction to I^2=0, Algebra Lemma 07C3, Lemmas lemma-lift-once and lemma-lift-twice)

proof.text: (Square-zero case: criterion.) In Steps 1-3 let $K\subset R$ be any ideal with $K^2=0$ such that $\Lambda/K\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/K$-algebras and $R\to\Lambda$ is flat; we show $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] whose underlying ring is a quotient $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ ($n\ge0$, $\mathfrak a$ an ideal); it is a set, each member is finitely presented (condition (i) of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]), and every smooth $R$-algebra is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a member of $\mathcal E$ (by (i)). By [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit] (Algebra, Lemma 07C3) applied to $\mathcal E$, it suffices to show: for every finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$ and homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\varphi:A\to\Lambda$ there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B'$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\to B'\to\Lambda$ composing to $\varphi$ (replace $B'$ by an isomorphic member of $\mathcal E$, transporting both maps along the isomorphism). The conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit] for this $\mathcal E$ is then exactly that $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Proposition Tag 07CM (proposition-lift, lines 1393-1418): 'We have to find a factorization A -> B -> Lambda with B smooth over R, see Algebra, Lemma 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit)'

proof.text: (Square-zero case: lift once.) Let $A$, $\varphi$ be as in Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-once] (Lemma 07CK; hypotheses $K^2=0$ and $\Lambda/K\Lambda$ a filtered colimit of smooth $R/K$-algebras) there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B$, a finitely generated ideal $J\subset KB$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\psi:A\to B/J$, $\chi:B/J\to\Lambda$ with $\chi\circ\psi=\varphi$. Let $\pi:B\to B/J$ be the quotient map and $\varphi_B=\chi\circ\pi:B\to\Lambda$, a homomorphism of $R$-algebras with $\varphi_B(J)=0$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Proposition Tag 07CM (proposition-lift, lines 1393-1418): 'By Lemma lemma-lift-once we may assume that A = B/J with B smooth over R and J in IB a finitely generated ideal'

proof.text: (Square-zero case: lift twice.) By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-twice] (Lemma 07CL; hypotheses $K^2=0$, $\Lambda/K\Lambda$ a filtered colimit of smooth $R/K$-algebras, $R\to\Lambda$ flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]) applied to $\varphi_B:B\to\Lambda$ and $J$ of Step 2, there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B'$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\alpha:B\to B'$, $\beta:B'\to\Lambda$ with $\alpha(J)=0$ and $\beta\circ\alpha=\varphi_B$. Since $\alpha(J)=0$, $\alpha=\bar\alpha\circ\pi$ for a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\bar\alpha:B/J\to B'$. Then $\beta\circ\bar\alpha\circ\pi=\varphi_B=\chi\circ\pi$ and $\pi$ is surjective, so $\beta\circ\bar\alpha=\chi$ and $\beta\circ(\bar\alpha\circ\psi)=\chi\circ\psi=\varphi$: $\varphi$ factors as $A\xrightarrow{\bar\alpha\psi}B'\xrightarrow{\beta}\Lambda$ with $B'$ smooth over $R$. By Step 1, $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Proposition Tag 07CM (proposition-lift, lines 1393-1418): 'By Lemma lemma-lift-twice we can find a commutative diagram ... such that alpha(J) = 0. Thus alpha factors as B -> A -> B''

proof.text: (Induction on $n$ with $I^n=0$; the source says only 'by induction on $n$ it suffices to consider the case $I^2=0$', written out here.) We show by induction on $n\ge1$: for all $R\to\Lambda$ and $I$ with $I^n=0$ satisfying (2) and (3), $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras. $n=1$: $I=0$, so $R/I=R$ and $\Lambda/I\Lambda=\Lambda$ as $R$-algebras, and (2) is the claim. $n=2$: Steps 1-3 with $K=I$. $n\ge3$, assuming the case $n-1$: put $K=I^{n-1}$; then $K^2=I^{2n-2}\subset I^n=0$ as $2n-2\ge n$, and $K\subset I$. Let $R'=R/K$, $\Lambda'=\Lambda/K\Lambda$ and $I'=I/K\subset R'$. (a) $(I')^{n-1}=(I^{n-1}+K)/K=0$. (b) $\Lambda'\cong R'\otimes_R\Lambda$ as $R'$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], which is a flat $R'$-module [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] since $\Lambda$ is a flat $R$-module by (3) [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; so $R'\to\Lambda'$ is flat. (c) $R'/I'=R/I$ and $\Lambda'/I'\Lambda'=\Lambda/(I\Lambda+K\Lambda)=\Lambda/I\Lambda$ (as $K\subset I$), compatibly with the algebra structures, so (2) holds for $R'\to\Lambda'$ and $I'$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Lambda/K\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/K$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Now Steps 1-3 for $R\to\Lambda$ and the square-zero ideal $K$ ($R\to\Lambda$ flat by (3)) show that $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
